Water excess or overhydration is rare and may be the result of 
inadequate output or excessive intake. Overhydration is charac-
terized by increased blood pressure; decreased pulse rate; edema; 
and decreased serum sodium, potassium, albumin, BUN, and 
creatinine values. Fluid restrictions may be necessary for certain 
medical conditions such as kidney or cardiac disease. For those 
on fluid restrictions, the fluid needs should be calculated on an 
individual basis. The usual diet provides approximately 1080 mL 
(36 oz), a little more than a quart of fluid per day.
Note: 3 oz is approximately 1⁄3 cup; 6 oz is approximately 2⁄3 cup.
